description: Adapting to Sea Level Rise and Coastal Erosion in Hawai'i is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); University of Hawai'i at Mānoa; Center for Island Climate Adaptation and Policy. Coastal erosion has been, and continues to be, a major issue in Hawaii. It is estimated that Oahu has lost 29% of its beaches from seawall construction resulting in beach erosion, while 72% of the beaches in Kauai are chronically eroding. Coverage: Honolulu, HI (2009). The toolkit gives Honolulu, HI as the location, 2009 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
